known_issues: Answer-key leak (DEBUG-HARDENING.md section 0): the composite starters used to ship Automate/docs/release-notes.md entries naming the reverted fixes. Verified for this task on the current tree: the four scored upstream entries and the haystack entry ('Fixed machines grabbing incubated eggs before they hatch') are absent from benchmarks/stardew-core/private/harbor/stardew-automate-release-regressions-v2/environment/StardewMods/Automate/docs/release-notes.md and from the Hub workspace; the engineered location-key pair never had an entry. The leak is therefore closed for the starter that E0 materialises (commit a483c85, which precedes the catalog 1.1.0 bump b5915a1; the prepared 1.1.0 image bakes the scrubbed notes too).

Report #224 (incubator egg theft) is public, real in the starter and fixed by gold.patch, but unscored. A submission that ignores it passes; the E0 alternative repairs it anyway. Probe probe-224-unfixed (reference with only that fix reverted; row kept in probes.tsv) was run in the real game and scores 100. It must stay outside both the target and the preserved set.

Reports #221 and #222 share one root cause (MachineGroupFactory.GetLocationKey and GameLocationNameComparer both use the bare Name). Only coops are built (benchmarks/stardew-core/private/harbor/stardew-automate-release-regressions-v2/tests/SuiteComposite.cs:226-252), so #222 is evidenced indirectly. 'machines in the first coop run' passes in the unchanged starter.

Report #216 never says the stuck output has an empty stack; the fixture produces the wedge only by setting heldObject.Stack = 0 (SuiteComposite.cs:166). DEBUG-HARDENING.md section 6 records the competing reading: 'a broken item' can be read as an item with missing data (the codebase has `catch (KeyNotFoundException) // invalid/broken item` in ChestContainer). A repair of that reading is rejected although the report as written admits it.

benchmarks/stardew-core/private/harbor/stardew-automate-release-regressions-v2/tests/SuiteComposite.cs:84 only asserts GetMachineStates(farm, whole map).Any() after 360 idle ticks. One reported tile (the shipping bin) satisfies it; the report's other location ('a shed full of kegs'), the completeness of the result ('all the machines that were missing') and the state values are never checked.

benchmarks/stardew-core/catalog.json:244-253 publishes a diagnosis the exam withholds (summary: '... engineered location-key defects', requirements: 'Handle duplicate building interiors without location identity collisions.', domains: 'identity'); the text is copied into the Hub's public tasks.json. The exam itself gives observations only.

The prepared evaluator image used for the E0 runs (sha256:3974e93bb723) bakes /opt/gcb/harness with the SuiteRunner that predates commit 276a070: there a throwing wait predicate is treated as SATISFIED (`return true`) instead of failing the case (repo version: benchmarks/stardew-core/private/harbor/harness/GcbHarness/Framework/SuiteRunner.cs:80-95). Predicates that can throw in this suite: ApiReportsGroup `_api!` (SuiteComposite.cs:117), MachineResumes `_brokenFurnace!` (:178), CoopAWorks/CoopBWorks `_coopAFurnace!`/`_coopBFurnace!` (:257, :264; null when the twin-coop setup case failed before assigning them). In each of them the statement after the wait dereferences the same null/throwing object, so the case still fails under the old runner; no spurious pass was found, but the image does not contain the fix the repository claims.
Case order is load-bearing: the second case of #211 and of #216 fails whenever the first one failed, and both coop cases fail if the coop setup fails.
